Shim & dispatcher (`main.rs`)\n- Dispatch on `argv[0]`: `cargo` → cargo tool profile; `gantry` → management CLI (full command set defined once in the “CLI surface” section below).\n- Real-binary resolution: config override `real_binary`, else PATH lookup with gantry's own shim dir stripped (self-recursion guard: refuse to exec a path whose canonical target is the gantry binary).\n- Passthrough path budget: no git/network/config-parse beyond a single mmap'd config read; target < 5 ms overhead.\n\n### 2. DecisionEngine\n- Intercept set from config (`[tool.cargo] intercept = [\"test\"]`).\n- Tier-0 (zero-config): with no config file present or `backend = \"none\"`, gantry is a pure local cap-wrapper — interception still applies the cgroup cap and full RunLog, nothing goes remote, and a `[gantry]` line notes the tier at most once per hour (state-file timestamp) so transcripts see it without per-run noise. Behavior is never derived from a half-parsed file — a broken gantry must never block builds, and must never rot silently either.\n\n### 3. GitGate\n- Checks in order, each with a printed reason on failure: inside work tree → `HEAD` resolves → configured remote exists → `git status --porcelain` empty.\n- All git interaction shells out to system `git` (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior, honors user's git config/credentials/hooks).\n\n### 4. RefPusher\n- `git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` (`ci_remote` defaults to `origin`); the epoch prefix is the GC lever (see below).\n- Push failure = InfraFailure → local fallback.\n- Optional `push_mode = \"branch\"` legacy escape hatch (explicit opt-in; prints a warning naming the risk).\n- GC (resolves Q-3 via leases): refs are named `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`; each run records a client-side lease (ref, run-id, expiry) in the state dir, and every successful push opportunistically sweeps remote refs whose epoch has expired and whose runs are terminal — no cron, no daemon, and a sweep can never delete a ref an in-flight run still holds a lease on. Each box sweeps only refs it created — lease records are local (see EC-09). The epoch-vs-content-addressing tension (the same sha pushed twice yields two refs) is settled by the design note required at Phase 1a entry.\n\n### 5. RemoteBackend trait + implementations\n\n```rust\ntrait RemoteBackend {\n    fn submit(&self, spec: &RunSpec) -> Result<RunHandle, BackendError>;\n    fn stream_logs(&self, h: &RunHandle, out: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<(), BackendError>; // best-effort\n    fn wait(&self, h: &RunHandle, deadline: Instant) -> Result<Verdict, BackendError>;     // authoritative\n---SECTION 1 (find_in_path / resolve context)---\n7:`gantry` is a transparent offload shim for expensive developer commands, cargo-first. GitGate\n- Checks in order, each with a printed reason on failure: inside work tree → `HEAD` resolves → configured remote exists → `git status --porcelain` empty.\n- All git interaction shells out to system `git` (no libgit2 — matches predecessor behavior, honors user's git config/credentials/hooks).\n\n### 4. RefPusher\n- `git push <ci_remote> <sha>:refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>` (`ci_remote` defaults to `origin`); the epoch prefix is the GC lever (see below).\n- Push failure = InfraFailure → local fallback.\n- Optional `push_mode = \"branch\"` legacy escape hatch (explicit opt-in; prints a warning naming the risk).\n- GC (resolves Q-3 via leases): refs are named `refs/gantry/<epoch>-<sha>`; each run records a client-side lease (ref, run-id, expiry) in the state dir, and every successful push opportunistically sweeps remote refs whose epoch has expired and whose runs are terminal — no cron, no daemon, and a sweep can never delete a ref an in-flight run still holds a lease on. Each box sweeps only refs it created — lease records are local (see EC-09). All filesystem errors (a directory unreadable, a permission\n/// denied on stat) surface as \"not a match\" for that entry — the walk continues\n/// to the next — because a single bad PATH slot must not abort the whole lookup.\n//\n// Held private by design (a resolve_real_binary-internal helper, like\n// shim_dir and strip_dir_from_path): only the in-module resolve_real_binary\n// (bf-614q) is meant to call it, and that consumer lands in the next child of\n// the chain — so find_in_path has no caller at this commit.\n// `#[allow(dead_code)]` keeps `-D warnings` green for the incremental build;\n// remove it once bf-614q gives the helper a caller.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nfn find_in_path(name: &str, path: &str) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, String> {\n    for entry in path.split(PATH_SEP) {\n        let candidate = std::path::Path::new(entry).join(name);\n        if is_executable_file(&candidate) {\n            return Ok(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    Err(format!(\n        \"gantry could not find `{name}` on PATH; install the real binary or set `real_binary`\"\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Whether `candidate` is an existing executable regular file.\n///\n/// `std::fs::metadata` (not `symlink_metadata`) follows a symlink to its target\n/// so a PATH entry pointing at a symlinked binary resolves correctly; a broken\n/// symlink, missing file, directory, or non-regular entry is a non-match. The\n/// executable check is platform-specific ([`is_executable`]).\nfn is_executable_file(candidate: &std::path::Path) -> bool {\n    // A stat failure (missing entry, permission denied) is a skip-not-fail: a\n    // stale or unreadable PATH slot must not abort the lookup.\n    let Ok(md) = std::fs::metadata(candidate) else {\n        return false;\n    };\n    md.is_file() && is_executable(candidate, &md)\n}\n\n/// Whether a regular file is executable.\n///\n/// Platform-specific because the notion differs: Unix consults the mode bits\n/// carried in [`std::fs::Metadata`]; Windows carries no execute bit and infers\n/// runnability from the file extension. Reads no environment (no `PATHEXT`) —\n/// the conventional executable extensions are fixed here so this helper honors\n/// the \"no env reads of its own\" contract shared with [`find_in_path`].\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn is_executable(_candidate: &std::path::Path, md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n    // Any execute bit (user/group/other) qualifies — matches shell PATH lookup,\n    // which treats a file runnable by anyone as found.\n    md.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0\n}\n\n#[cfg(windows)]\nfn is_executable(candidate: &std::path::Path, _md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n    matches!(\n        candidate.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()),\n        Some(\"exe\") | Some(\"bat\") | Some(\"cmd\") | Some(\"com\")\n    )\n}\n```\n\nWait, there's a subtlety with clippy.
